title: 296. 5 steps to becoming an assertive communicator

sentences.en: Other people collect perfume bottles or coffee mugs or overseas banknotes, classic sweaters from the 80s.
sentences.zh: 其他人则收集香水瓶、咖啡马克杯、海外纸币，或是80年代的经典毛衣。

sentences.zh: 收藏是一件极其私人的事。

sentences.zh: 山姆将带你探索那些构成我们自身的记忆、执念与微小珍宝。

sentences.zh: 《魅力山姆·托德》。

sentences.zh: 这是Pandora呈献的故事要讲栏目。

sentences.zh: 立即在iHeart上收听该播客。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落，非常高兴你能回来收听又一期节目，当然，我们要在这里剖析属于我们二十几岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Today, we are talking about an episode that was requested by so many of you after an episode I did maybe a year ago even on how to have better conversations.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要聊的话题，是一年多前我做过一期关于如何进行更好对话的节目后，许多听众一直强烈要求的。

sentences.en: And in that episode, I alluded to this idea of different kind of communication types, one of them being an assertive communicator.
sentences.zh: 在当时那期节目中，我暗示了不同沟通类型的概念，其中之一就是“自信型沟通者”。

sentences.en: And so in this episode, I want to circle back onto that.
sentences.zh: 所以在本期节目中，我想回过头来探讨这个话题。

sentences.en: I want to circle back to this idea and talk about how you can be an assertive communicator.
sentences.zh: 我想重拾这个理念，并谈谈你该如何成为一个自信的沟通者。

sentences.en: How can someone become someone who is confident in what they have and confident in what they're saying using some pretty amazing principles of psychology?
sentences.zh: 如何运用一些极其出色的心理学原理，让自己变得既对自己的观点充满信心、又对所说的话底气十足？

sentences.en: So many of you have asked, when is this episode coming?
sentences.zh: 你们当中有很多人都在问，这期节目什么时候播？

sentences.en: And I honestly kept putting it on the back burner and like delaying it for whatever reason.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我一直把它搁置一旁，出于各种原因一拖再拖。

sentences.en: But this week, I don't know what it was.
sentences.zh: 但不知为何，就在本周，

sentences.en: It really felt like the week to finally break it down.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得是时候终于把这个话题拆解清楚了。

sentences.en: So today, we're going to go through my five tips to be an assertive communicator, but also just a convincing, persuasive communicator in general.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，我们将探讨我总结的成为自信沟通者的五个技巧，同时也会探讨如何总体上成为一个有说服力的沟通者。

sentences.en: It's so interesting to me because we are never really taught how to be persuasive or how to ask for what we want in a way that will actually get us what we want,
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得非常有趣，因为我们从未真正被教导过如何去说服别人，或者如何以一种真正能让我们如愿以偿的方式去表达诉求，

sentences.en: but also not frustrate people or make someone angry or upset.
sentences.zh: 同时又不会让人感到沮丧、生气或心烦。

sentences.en: Sure, you know, maybe we did public speaking in high school.
sentences.zh: 当然，也许你在高中时上过公众演讲课。

sentences.en: Maybe you did like debating and you had to get up and give a speech.
sentences.zh: 也许你参加过辩论赛之类，必须站起来发表演讲。

sentences.en: But from my memory, when I did those things, you would kind of get up and do it and then they would grade you on the skills you already had
sentences.zh: 但在我的记忆中，当我做这些事情的时候，你基本上就是站上去讲完，然后他们会根据你原本就具备的技能给你打分，

sentences.en: without really giving you an opportunity to improve.
sentences.zh: 并没有真正给你提供提升的机会。

sentences.en: Like I cannot actually remember anyone giving me legitimate tips or a course.
sentences.zh: 比如我实在想不起有谁给过我实质性的技巧指导或开过什么课程。

sentences.en: It was just being judged on like your pre-existing ability and that pre-existing ability, how we communicate is largely formed by our parents,
sentences.zh: 我们只是在被评判你原有的能力，而这种原有的能力以及我们的沟通方式，很大程度上是由我们的父母塑造的，

sentences.en: how they communicated, what their professions were, your innate confidence level.
sentences.zh: 包括他们的沟通方式、他们的职业，以及你与生俱来的自信水平。

sentences.en: But being an assertive communicator, it can be taught.
sentences.zh: 但自信的沟通是可以被教导的。

sentences.en: It is not just for people who are inherently self-assured.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅属于那些天生自信的人。

sentences.en: It's also not just for extroverts either.
sentences.zh: 它也不仅仅属于外向者。

sentences.en: It's for people who are introverts.
sentences.zh: 它同样属于内向的人。

sentences.en: It's for people who are shy.
sentences.zh: 属于害羞的人。

sentences.en: It's for people who are people pleasers.
sentences.zh: 属于习惯讨好他人的人。

sentences.en: And it's a really valuable skill to have.
sentences.zh: 这是一项非常有价值的技能。

sentences.en: I think it's one of those skills that should probably be mandatory.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一项应该被列为必修课的技能。

sentences.en: Like I always think that in high school, we need to have like an intro to life 101 course.
sentences.zh: 我总是觉得，在高中里我们需要开设一门类似“生活入门101”的课程。

sentences.en: And in that course, you know, you should learn about taxes.
sentences.zh: 在这门课里，你应该了解纳税知识。

sentences.en: You should learn about how to find a good mechanic, how to set boundaries, financial literacy.
sentences.zh: 你应该学习如何找到靠谱的修理工、如何设定边界以及财务素养。

sentences.en: And I think you should also learn how to be an assertive communicator.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你还应该学习如何成为一个自信的沟通者。

sentences.en: There is not a single profession that does not require it.
sentences.zh: 没有哪一个职业是不需要这项技能的。

sentences.en: And recent research that I was finding when I was investigating this topic has also discovered that being an assertive communicator, it doesn't just help relationships.
sentences.zh: 我在研究这个主题时发现的最新研究也表明，做一个自信的沟通者不仅有助于改善人际关系。

sentences.en: It doesn't just help you in your career, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然，它不仅对你的职业生涯有帮助。

sentences.en: It also makes you less stressed.
sentences.zh: 它还能让你减轻压力。

sentences.en: It reduces cortisol arousal.
sentences.zh: 它能减少皮质醇的激发。

sentences.en: It makes you healthier.
sentences.zh: 它能让你更健康。

sentences.en: It makes you healthier as an individual.
sentences.zh: 它能让你作为个体变得更加健康。

sentences.en: So I'm going to give you five scientifically founded and psychologically backed tips to help you not feel ashamed for asking for what you want, how to make your preferences known,
sentences.zh: 所以，我要给你们五个基于科学和心理学支撑的技巧，帮助你们不再为争取自己想要的东西而感到羞耻，教你们如何表达自己的偏好，

sentences.en: how to be someone who others will listen to, and just so much more.
sentences.zh: 如何成为一个能让人听进去话的人，以及更多内容。

sentences.en: So without further ado, my lovely listeners, let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 闲话少说，可爱的听众们，我们这就开始吧。

sentences.en: Let's begin by just really articulating what an assertive communicator is, because I have already alluded to the fact that it's likely different
sentences.zh: 让我们首先来明确什么是自信的沟通者，因为我刚才已经暗示过，它可能与

sentences.en: to what you are currently imagining.
sentences.zh: 你目前想象的有所不同。

sentences.en: So researchers largely agree that there are four different communication styles when it comes to tone and attitude.
sentences.zh: 研究人员大体上一致认为，就语气和态度而言，存在四种不同的沟通风格。

sentences.en: There is passive, there is aggressive, there is passive aggressive, and there is assertive.
sentences.zh: 它们分别是：被动型、攻击型、被动攻击型和自信型。

sentences.en: Assertive sometimes in our minds can be confused with aggressive.
sentences.zh: 在我们脑海中，自信有时可能会与攻击性混淆。

sentences.en: We assume that it might come off as domineering, demanding, selfish, loud, arrogant, like I want this, I want it now.
sentences.zh: 我们以为它可能会显得专横、苛求、自私、大嗓门、傲慢，就像“我想要这个，我现在就要”。

sentences.en: If I don't get it, we will have issues.
sentences.zh: “如果我得不到，我们就有麻烦了。”

sentences.en: There is no compromise.
sentences.zh: 根本没有妥协的余地。

sentences.en: Assertive communication really means that you advocate for yourself.
sentences.zh: 而自信沟通实际上意味着你是在为自己发声。

sentences.en: You don't self-silence, and you try and get your point across honestly, and with kindness, but also self-assurance.
sentences.zh: 你不会自我消声，并且你试图以诚实、友善但又不失自信的方式把你的观点表达清楚。

sentences.en: It sounds like I'm going to invite you to see it from my perspective.
sentences.zh: 听起来就像是我邀请你从我的角度来看待问题。

sentences.en: It would help the team if you did this.
sentences.zh: 如果你这样做，会对团队有所帮助。

sentences.en: I would appreciate if you didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 如果你不那样做，我会很感激的。

sentences.en: I'm going to sit with this one.
sentences.zh: 我要先冷静下来琢磨一下这件事。

sentences.en: I'm going to think about this because I'm not feeling it currently.
sentences.zh: 我要考虑一下，因为我目前没有这种感觉。

sentences.en: There is actually a lot of joy and a lot of peace in being an assertive communicator because I think implicitly you understand that not everyone is going to agree with you.
sentences.zh: 作为一个自信的沟通者，其实能收获很多快乐与平静，因为你内心里明白，并不是每个人都会同意你的观点。

sentences.en: Not everyone is going to do what you want them to do, but you have made your point.
sentences.zh: 并不是每个人都会按你的意愿去做事，但你已经表达了你的观点。

sentences.en: You have communicated it, and that sits really well with you.
sentences.zh: 你已经传达出去了，这让你感到非常坦然。

sentences.en: An assertive communicator is oftentimes
sentences.zh: 一个自信的沟通者往往

sentences.en: actually the most persuasive because they also don't use threats.
sentences.zh: 其实是最具说服力的，因为他们不使用威胁。

sentences.en: They don't use guilt.
sentences.zh: 他们不使用负罪感。

sentences.en: They don't use demands to get their point across.
sentences.zh: 他们不通过无理要求来表达观点。

sentences.en: They use inspiration.
sentences.zh: 他们用的是启发。

sentences.en: They use encouragement.
sentences.zh: 他们用的是鼓励。

sentences.en: They use personality.
sentences.zh: 他们用的是个性。

sentences.en: Another defining point is that they often rely on nonverbal cues that are very welcoming and which activate people's mirror neurons,
sentences.zh: 另一个明显的特点是，他们经常依赖非常热情且能激活人们镜像神经元的非语言线索，

sentences.en: which we're going to speak about in just a second, but the research has shown that this ability is really what makes assertive communicators so persuasive,
sentences.zh: 我们马上就会谈到这点，但研究表明，这种能力正是使自信沟通者如此具有说服力的关键所在，

sentences.en: and they do things that people don't often think are persuasive.
sentences.zh: 而且他们会做一些人们通常不认为具有说服力的事。

sentences.en: They speak slower.
sentences.zh: 他们说话语速更慢。

sentences.en: They also use more of their vocal range.
sentences.zh: 他们还更善于运用自己的音域。

sentences.en: Side note, this was quite an interesting piece of research that I discovered when I was looking into this, and it's that people with more empathy
sentences.zh: 顺便一提，这是我在研究这个课题时发现的一个非常有趣的科研成果，那就是更有同理心的人

sentences.en: also tend to use more of their vocal range, and a paper from 2009 actually found that diagnosed psychopaths actually have a reduced vocal range, so their voice is more immovable.
sentences.zh: 往往也会使用更广的音域。2009年的一篇论文实际上发现，被诊断为精神病态的人音域反而较窄，因此他们的声音更加死板。

sentences.en: It doesn't flow.
sentences.zh: 它没有起伏。

sentences.en: It doesn't go up and down.
sentences.zh: 它不会上下波动。

sentences.en: So there you go.
sentences.zh: 所以你看。

sentences.en: A really interesting sign of both an assertive and empathetic person, but also communicator.
sentences.zh: 这是无论是自信且富有同理心的人，还是自信沟通者的一个非常有趣的标志。

sentences.en: They use their voice.
sentences.zh: 他们会运用自己的声音。

sentences.en: They use it almost like an instrument, something that flows and surrounds people, and I really don't think that being assertive and being empathetic
sentences.zh: 他们几乎把声音当成一件乐器来用，一种能够流淌并包裹人们的声音。而且我真的认为，自信与富有同理心

sentences.en: is something that can be separated.
sentences.zh: 是无法被剥离开来的。

sentences.en: They actually go hand in hand.
sentences.zh: 它们其实是相辅相成的。

sentences.en: Let's talk about the other three types of communicators.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈其他三种类型的沟通者。

sentences.en: Aggressive communicators, they are forceful.
sentences.zh: 攻击型沟通者，他们十分强势。

sentences.en: They are immovable.
sentences.zh: 他们油盐不进。

sentences.en: They interrupt.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢打断别人。

sentences.en: They yell.
sentences.zh: 他们大喊大叫。

sentences.en: They use threats.
sentences.zh: 他们使用威胁。

sentences.en: They find it hard to be silent.
sentences.zh: 他们很难保持沉默。

sentences.en: They also use less eye contact.
sentences.zh: 他们也较少有眼神交流。

sentences.en: Passive communicators are often very indirect and submissive.
sentences.zh: 被动型沟通者通常非常间接且顺从。

sentences.en: They really just avoid expressing their needs and they downplay their feelings and they avoid conflict.
sentences.zh: 他们极力回避表达自己的需求，淡化自己的感受，并逃避冲突。

sentences.en: It's also highly associated with people who are conflict averse or who are chronic people pleasers, chronic apologizers as well, which we actually have an episode about
sentences.zh: 这也高度关联于那些逃避冲突的人，或者那些长期讨好型人格、习惯性道歉的人，对此我们实际上有一期节目

sentences.en: coming up very, very soon.
sentences.zh: 很快就要播出了。

sentences.en: And finally, passive aggressive communicators.
sentences.zh: 最后是被动攻击型沟通者。

sentences.en: This is the least successful communicator and that's because it combines the worst aspects of the two previous communication stars.
sentences.zh: 这是最不成功的沟通者，因为集成了前两种沟通风格最糟糕的方面。

sentences.en: They are often hostile.
sentences.zh: 他们通常抱有敌意。

sentences.en: They are indirect.
sentences.zh: 他们表达委婉含蓄。

sentences.en: They don't say what they mean.
sentences.zh: 他们话里有话、言不由衷。

sentences.en: They rely heavily on silence, the silent treatment, and also guilt to support their unrealistic demands.
sentences.zh: 他们极其依赖沉默、冷暴力，以及负罪感来支撑他们不切实际的要求。

sentences.en: So those are the four communication stars and we often begin to develop our communication style not through an intentional effort, but through outside influence.
sentences.zh: 这就是四种沟通风格。我们往往不是通过刻意努力，而是通过外界影响来形成我们的沟通风格。

sentences.en: So family, culture, early experiences, our environment, which is actually a good thing.
sentences.zh: 比如家庭、文化、早期经历、我们的环境，这其实是一件好事。

sentences.en: I know it sounds like, oh, none of this is within my control, but it also means that a lot of it is environmental, so it can be changed.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来好像“啊，这些都不受我控制”，但这也意味着其中很多因素都属于环境范畴，因此是可以改变的。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's talk about how we can change them.
sentences.zh: 闲话少说，我们来谈谈如何改变它们。

sentences.en: Let's talk about those five tips I spoke about before.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈我之前提到的那五个技巧。

sentences.en: So my first tip for becoming an assertive communicator, tip one, is that assertive communicators know how to value silence more than their words.
sentences.zh: 因此，我关于如何成为一个自信沟通者的第一个技巧，即技巧一，是自信的沟通者懂得如何让沉默比语言更有价值。

sentences.en: And it doesn't mean they use the silent treatment.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着他们使用冷暴力。

sentences.en: It means they appreciate the pause.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们懂得欣赏停顿。

sentences.en: Pausing in a conversation actually brings you back into control.
sentences.zh: 在对话中进行停顿实际上能让你重新掌控主动权。

sentences.en: Now, I don't think that conversations are necessarily like a battlefield
sentences.zh: 现在，我不认为对话一定像是一个为了

sentences.en: for being in charge and it's like this huge conflict.
sentences.zh: 争夺主导权而展开的战场，也不认为这是一场巨大的冲突。

sentences.en: But a pause, I think, brings you back into control over yourself, which is what's really essential here.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，停顿能让你重新掌控自己，这才是真正核心的关键所在。

sentences.en: Have you ever, I don't know, have you ever had that experience of being in a really important conversation with someone
sentences.zh: 你有没有过这种经历，我是说，你有没有过这种体验：在和某人进行一次非常重要的对话时，

sentences.en: and you find you just can't stop talking?
sentences.zh: 你发现自己根本停不下来？

sentences.en: Like, words are just spilling out of your mouth before you can even think of them.
sentences.zh: 就像话语源源不断地从嘴里涌出来，甚至不等你的大脑思考。

sentences.en: Like, there is no, there is nothing between your brain and the words coming out of your mouth.

sentences.en: A, it would have shown the interviewers that I was actually considering their question a little bit and B, I would have answered better.

sentences.en: I think a lot of us are innately very afraid of silence in a conversation but pausing really just ensures that you say what you mean.
sentences.zh: 我想我们很多人天生都非常害怕对话中的沉默，但停顿确实能确保你言之有物。

sentences.en: And there's this other part of that as well, pauses, silence, that is where meaning takes hold.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，还有另一个层面：停顿和沉默，正是意义沉淀的地方。

sentences.en: It is really hard to know what someone really means or is saying in a conversation if you are constantly talking and having to make these assessments on the fly.
sentences.zh: 如果你一直在说话，必须得在飞行中不断做出这些评估，你就很难知道别人在对话中真正意味着什么或在说些什么。

sentences.en: This is why I think we typically only fully realise what someone was actually saying to us after a conversation is over.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为，通常只有在对话结束之后，我们才能完全领会别人对我们到底说了什么。

sentences.en: And sometimes that's really frustrating because suddenly like you have all your best comebacks, like you think of all the things that you wish you had said.
sentences.zh: 有时候这真的很令人沮丧，因为突然之间你所有的绝妙回击都涌上心头，你想起了所有你希望当时能说出口的话。

sentences.en: Pauses are so effective in that sense because you can really hear the things that aren't being said.

sentences.en: And it also says
sentences.zh: 它同时也传达出

sentences.en: I'm comfortable with silence because I'm comfortable with myself, which is a particularly powerful message that you want to send if you're trying to be assertive and you're trying

sentences.en: to advocate for yourself.

sentences.en: So here's how to apply this practically.

sentences.en: When you feel yourself getting very, maybe running away with your thoughts or you're reaching dead ends or you feel like you're losing control of the conversation, pause for three
sentences.zh: 当你觉得情绪有些失控，思绪或许开始飘忽，或者陷入死胡同，又或者你觉得自己快要掌控不住这场对话时，请在每句话开口之前暂停三

sentences.en: seconds before every sentence before you say anything or you can create a physical cue that you need to do first before you speak.
sentences.zh: 秒钟，或者在说话前先做一个你习惯的肢体动作。

sentences.en: I was reading this really amazing book recently, I cannot remember the name, but the author talks about how she always nods her head twice before replying to someone.
sentences.zh: 我最近读了一本非常棒的书，书名记不清了，但作者提到她每次在回复别人之前，都会习惯性地点头两次。

sentences.en: So someone will say something to her and she'll go and then she'll reply because it positively reinforces that she's listening but it also allows her to reassess her words.
sentences.zh: 所以当别人对她说话时，她会先点头，然后再回应，因为这不仅能积极强化她在认真倾听的信号，还能让她有机会重新斟酌自己的言辞。

sentences.en: Assertive communicators, they know the power of the pause.
sentences.zh: 自信的沟通者，他们懂得暂停的力量。

sentences.en: Tip number two, learn how to regulate your body.
sentences.zh: 第二招，学会调节你的身体。

sentences.en: It is just as important as what you have to say.
sentences.zh: 这和你要说的话同样重要。

sentences.en: Your body language is language.

sentences.en: It is saying something and if you feel like you're about to burst out of your skin or there is this hidden tension that you can't control, most of the time that will come
sentences.zh: 它在传递信息，如果你觉得自己浑身不自在，或者有一种无法控制的隐形紧张感，这种状态大多数时候都会

sentences.en: We're going to regulate that.

sentences.en: Before you go into a conversation or you go to do a speech or whatever it is, I want you to do this exercise with me that I personally use.
sentences.zh: 在你开始一场对话、准备进行演讲，或者做任何类似的事情之前，我想让你和我一起做这个我个人一直在用的练习。

sentences.en: This is the exact exercise I do before.
sentences.zh: 这就是我在上场前雷打不动会做的练习。

sentences.en: Every speech, every podcast recording, every live show, it is an excellent way to regulate your body.
sentences.zh: 每一次演讲、每一次录播客、每一场直播，这都是调节身体的绝佳方法。

sentences.en: So you stand up, you let your arms go completely slack, you let your shoulders fall as far as they want to, as far as they can without any effort.
sentences.zh: 首先，站直身体，让双臂完全放松下垂，让双肩自然下垂，放到它们不用费力就能达到的最低位置。

sentences.en: Then I want you to notice your eyebrows, notice your forehead,
sentences.zh: 接着，留意你的眉毛，留意你的额头，

sentences.en: release any tension, consciously release the muscles around your mouth, around your eyes, just let them go as well.
sentences.zh: 释放所有的紧张感，有意识地放松你嘴巴周围、眼睛周围的肌肉，让它们也彻底放松。

sentences.en: And I want you to sway gently from side to side, maybe hum to yourself, keep your eyes closed, roll your shoulders back, then forward, take three deep breaths, and open your eyes.
sentences.zh: 然后，我希望你轻轻地左右摇晃身体，也许可以自己哼点小曲，闭上眼睛，双肩向后转动，再向前转动，深呼吸三次，最后睁开眼睛。

sentences.en: This exercise works because of the principles of progressive relaxation.
sentences.zh: 这个练习之所以有效，是因为它遵循了渐进式放松的原理。

sentences.en: It makes you feel more in touch with your body, it means that you can regulate it, it means you have a baseline level of stability, but that ritual is also equally soothing, so it
sentences.zh: 它能让你更好地感知自己的身体，意味着你能对其进行调节，让你拥有一个基准水平的稳定性，而且这种仪式感同样具有舒缓作用，所以它

sentences.en: literally years analysing over

sentences.en: 5,000 successful public speakers, and he has noticed that there is a few things that they really do, and which you might not notice they're doing, but you are nonetheless being
sentences.zh: 5000名优秀的公众演讲者，他发现这些人有一些共同的做法，你可能不会注意到他们在这么做，但你无形中却在受到

sentences.en: influenced by.
sentences.zh: 他们的影响。

sentences.en: So the first thing they do is that they stop themselves from hunching, they keep their shoulders back, they open up their body, it invites people in, they raise their chin,
sentences.zh: 所以他们做的第一件事就是克服驼背，保持双肩向后展，敞开身体，这会给人一种欢迎的姿态；他们会抬起下巴，

sentences.en: they also lean towards whoever they're speaking to, which actually gives the impression of confidence and feeling relaxed as opposed to tension and leaning away.
sentences.zh: 而且身体会向谈话对象倾斜，这实际上会给人一种自信和放松的印象，而不是表现出紧张和向后退缩。

sentences.en: If you think about it in nature, if you're turning away from someone, if you're moving away from them, you feel threatened.
sentences.zh: 仔细想想，在自然界中，如果你把身体转开，如果你从别人身边退缩，说明你感到了威胁。

sentences.en: If you're leaning towards them, you feel safe and that makes someone else feel safe.
sentences.zh: 如果你向前倾身，说明你感到安全，这也会让对方感到安全。

sentences.en: Two other things that they do, the first thing is that successful assertive communicators tilt their head.
sentences.zh: 他们还会做另外两件事，第一件就是，自信的沟通者会歪着头。

sentences.zh: 想象一下，当有人对你诉说一件非常非常悲伤、非常非常糟糕的事情，比如说，我不知道，我得了癌症，或者我刚被男朋友甩了。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm so sorry.

sentences.en: Oh, that's so awful.

sentences.en: Because for some reason, it's an indicator of empathy.

sentences.en: It's a silent way of displaying, like,
sentences.zh: 这是一种无声的方式，仿佛在说：

sentences.en: I'm thinking about you, I care about you.

sentences.zh: 现在，自信的沟通者会做的最后一件事，

sentences.en: David Phillips noticed was something called a
sentences.zh: 大卫·菲利普斯注意到的是一种叫做

sentences.en: Duchenne smile.
sentences.zh: 杜兴微笑（Duchenne smile）的表情。

sentences.en: So a Duchenne smile is a type of genuine grin that moves somebody's entire face, not just their mouth.
sentences.zh: 所以，杜兴微笑是一种发自内心的微笑，它会带动一个人整张脸的肌肉，而不仅仅是嘴巴。

sentences.en: So this kind of smile, it was discovered, or I should say, first named by a French neurologist called
sentences.zh: 这种微笑最早是被一位名叫

sentences.zh: 其中一种调动了你脸部、额头、眼睛周围以及嘴巴周围的所有肌肉。

sentences.en: The other smile, the non-Duchenne smile, just uses your mouth.
sentences.zh: 另一种微笑，即非杜兴微笑，只动用了嘴巴。

sentences.en: It's a very inauthentic kind of smile, a very coy kind of smile.
sentences.zh: 那是一种非常不真诚的微笑，一种带着羞涩的微笑。

sentences.en: If you think about the Mona Lisa, best example of a non-Duchenne smile.

sentences.en: But what they have found after the naming of this smile is that people who present a

sentences.en: Duchenne smile, it serves a really important function.
sentences.zh: 杜兴微笑其实具有非常重要的功能。

sentences.en: It makes you seem more friendly, it makes you more likable, people are more likely to agree with you, and it just makes you seem like a more assertive, kind person.

sentences.en: And this is the work of what we call mirror neurons.

sentences.en: And what it does is when someone else performs an action to you, this part of your brain, these cells, automatically are firing.

sentences.en: And it essentially wants to perform that action back to that person.
sentences.zh: 它本质上会促使你想对对方做出同样的动作。

sentences.en: Someone smiles, you find yourself smiling.
sentences.zh: 别人笑了，你会发现自己也笑了。

sentences.en: Someone looks disgusted, you find yourself also looking disgusted.
sentences.zh: 别人露出厌恶的表情，你会发现自己也露出了厌恶的表情。

sentences.en: It's this kind of
sentences.zh: 这是一种

sentences.en: weird neurological way that we feel connected and bonded to each other through that exchange of behaviors.

sentences.en: And so if you want to really be assertive and if you want to be convincing, what you have to do is perform the kind of body language that you think or you wish someone was going to

sentences.en: Okay, we're talking about the five ways to transform yourself into an assertive communicator.

sentences.en: Tip number three, make it about you.

sentences.en: If you want something done or you want to convince someone of some kind of point, it's actually not about them.
sentences.zh: 如果你想办成某件事，或者想让别人信服某种观点，其实重点并不在于对方。

sentences.en: We also want to switch from people-pleasing to something called self-authorship.
sentences.zh: 我们还希望从迎合他人转变为一种名为“自我署名”（self-authorship）的概念。

sentences.en: Self-authorship is not demanding, it just works to articulate our perspective, our self-concept, by essentially using phrases that reflect our self-definition.
sentences.zh: “自我署名”并非提出无理要求，它只是致力于阐明我们的视角、我们的自我概念，其核心就是使用那些能够反映我们自我定义的短语。

sentences.en: And it uses these phrases as a way to say, hey, humanize me, know that I'm my own person, know that I respect myself, but I want to work with you on that.
